Three offices · One brokerage

Reach a real broker, on the first call.

We do not run a referral desk. The number you dial connects to whoever picks up — and whoever picks up is a licensed broker who can answer the question. Whether you are buying, selling, or trying to make sense of a property you already own, write to us below or call the office nearest you.

General Inquiry

Tell us what you are looking for.

Short, long, or just thinking out loud — write the message that makes sense and we will figure out who is best to reply. Most messages get a response within one business day.

FAQ

Questions we get a lot.

If yours is not here, write us. We will answer plainly.

We work the corridor from Beacon up through Hudson and west into the Catskills. Specifically: Rhinebeck, Red Hook, Tivoli, Hudson, Catskill, Athens, Saugerties, Kingston, New Paltz, Stone Ridge, Beacon, and Cold Spring. If a property is outside that range we will likely refer you to a broker we trust nearby rather than try to stretch our coverage.

We start with a no-fee, no-obligation consultation — usually a 45-minute call or coffee — to understand what you are looking for, what the budget actually is, and what your timeline looks like. From there we sign a standard buyer representation agreement that lays out our role clearly. Our commission is paid by the seller in most transactions; if not, we will tell you that upfront.

One of us comes out, walks the property, and stays for a long conversation. We look at the comps, talk through what needs to happen to prepare for market, and tell you honestly what we think the right list price is — not the price that wins the listing. If we agree to represent the property, we cover professional photography, staging consultation, and marketing through our network and field-notes audience.

Yes, particularly the kind of mixed-use buildings common to Warren Street in Hudson and the village cores of Rhinebeck and Beacon — storefronts with apartments above, small adaptive-reuse projects, the occasional small office building. We do not handle ground-up commercial development or pure investment portfolios.

Often, yes. A meaningful share of what we sell is what the market would call "needs work" — historic houses with deferred maintenance, properties with unconventional layouts, the occasional honest fixer. We will be straight with you about what the renovation likely costs, what it likely returns at sale, and what the right list price is given the condition. That conversation tends to be the first real one we have with a seller.
